transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey, Dr. [Name]. I'm here because, well, I feel like I'm just always running hot, you know? Like I can't shut the motor off. And lately, that's been getting me into some real trouble at the firehouse. Which is crazy because I love the firehouse. The guys there are great. We actually had this massive chili cook-off last weekend—Miller makes this insane ghost pepper one, absolutely destroys your stomach, but you can't stop eating it. Anyway, my wife says I've been like this since we met, just always go-go-go, but it's really starting to mess with my job now.

Thinking back to when you were a kid, say before age 12, did you already have that same restless, motor-always-running feeling, or is this something that started later, like in your teens or adulthood?

Oh, definitely not a new thing. My mom says I was exactly like this back in grade school, too. She said I was always out of my seat, blurting out answers, losing my homework... which is hilarious because I actually *did* have a dog eat my homework once. Buster. He was this massive golden retriever mix, best dog ever, but he chewed right through my math workbook in third grade. My teacher, Mrs. Gable—she was super strict, always wore these intense puffy-paint sweatshirts—she totally didn't believe me. She was always sending notes home to my parents anyway, saying I was bright enough to do the work but just wouldn't settle down. But yeah, Buster completely destroyed that workbook. He used to chew on the baseboards in the kitchen too, actually, which drove my dad absolutely insane because he had just redone the floors... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being a kid. But yeah, my mom says I've been this way forever.
Has your wife, family, or coworkers ever described you as getting into fights, breaking rules, being aggressive, or defying authority, beyond just being restless or impulsive?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I'm not a violent guy. I don't get into fights or, like, break the law or anything. I actually really respect the rules, especially at the station. You have to, right? Like, if you don't follow protocol on a call, someone could get seriously hurt. We had this one call last month, a three-alarm fire at this old warehouse downtown. The place was a total maze, and the roof was already starting to sag when we rolled up. Captain told us to stay exterior, and let me tell you, that was the right call because not ten minutes later, the whole back section just collapsed. Sounded like a freight train crashing through the building. The dust cloud was so thick you couldn't see the rig. We were out there for like fourteen hours straight. My gear smelled like burnt rubber for a week, and my wife actually made me leave it in the garage because it was stinking up the laundry room. She's got this super sensitive nose, like, she can smell if I had onions for lunch from across the house. It's wild. But yeah, no, I don't go around breaking rules or getting aggressive with people. Just... just the restlessness, really.
Aside from the restlessness, do you also struggle with things like losing focus during tasks, forgetting appointments or instructions, or having trouble staying organized at work or home?

Yeah, man, losing focus is... it's bad. Like, when we have morning briefings at the station, or if we're doing drone training? I’m completely locked in for the first few minutes. I'm nodding, I'm looking at the screen. But then, I don't know, I suddenly realize I’ve just been staring at the map or the monitor and I didn’t catch half of what command just said. 

Which is bad with the drones, especially. Speaking of drones, my brother-in-law just bought one of those crazy expensive DJI ones for his photography business. He does weddings mostly, and he actually took it down to Cabo for a shoot last month. Get this—the drone got completely dive-bombed by a seagull. Like, full-on attacked right over the ocean. They lost the drone, the memory card, all the footage of the ceremony. The bride was absolutely furious, which, you know, I get, but also, what are you gonna do? It's a wild bird! Birds near the beach are just fearless. When my wife and I went to Florida for our honeymoon, a pelican literally snatched a whole hotdog right out of my hand while I was walking on the boardwalk. Scared the living daylights out of me. We ended up having to eat at this little crab shack instead, which actually had the best garlic fries I've ever... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Oh, right, staying focused. But yeah, I definitely zone out a lot during instructions and stuff.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, finishing other people's sentences, or having trouble waiting your turn in line or during discussions?

Oh, yeah, all the time. It’s actually kind of a problem at work. Like, if the other firefighters are talking through a plan or figuring out how we're gonna tackle a drill, I just cut right in. It’s like the answer is already in my head, so I just say it, and then a second later I realize I totally stepped on somebody or messed up the whole flow of the discussion. I just can't wait for them to get to the point. 

Waiting in general is just... ugh. Like waiting in line at the grocery store when I'm buying food for the station. We take turns cooking, right? And last week I was making my famous three-bean chili. Which, by the way, won second place at the county cook-off two years ago. First place went to this guy from Engine 42 who put smoked brisket in his, which honestly feels like cheating. Brisket makes literally anything taste amazing. My dad used to smoke brisket for like eighteen hours in our backyard when I was a kid. He actually built his own smoker out of a steel drum. Welded the hinges himself, painted it with this high-heat engine enamel... he was always tinkering with stuff like that in the garage. He actually restored a '69 Mustang from just a rusted-out shell he found in a barn. Beautiful car, cherry red with these white racing stripes. Man, I loved that car. He ended up selling it to pay for my sister's wedding, which she didn't even appreciate because they got divorced three years later anyway... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, interrupting people. Yeah, I definitely do that. I just blurt things out before they're done speaking.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports lifelong, cross-situational symptoms of both inattention (losing focus during briefings, zoning out, tangential thought derailment) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (constant restlessness, interrupting conversations, difficulty waiting turn), with childhood onset confirmed by maternal report (out-of-seat behavior, blurting answers, losing homework before age 12). Symptoms cause functional impairment in both occupational (firehouse briefings, drills, teamwork) and marital domains. No evidence of conduct disorder, oppositional defiance, aggression, or rule-breaking, ruling out F90.1 and comorbid conduct disorder. Presence of both inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptom clusters (rather than one alone) supports combined presentation (F90.2) over predominantly inattentive (F90.0) type.
